podcast.title: Death from Brain Tumour (1971)
podcast.body: Junia Parker's career ended with his death from a brain tumour in 1971. "until shortly before his death from a brain tumour in 1971."

podcast.title: Backing Rufus Thomas
podcast.body: Junia Parker and The Blue Flames backed Rufus Thomas on his song "Tigerman," which Elvis Presley would later perform in the 1960s and as a medley with "Mystery Train" in the 1970s. "Parker and his blue flames also backed Rufus Thomas on Tigerman."

podcast.title: Collaboration with Howlin' Wolf
podcast.body: Before forming his own band, Parker worked with Howlin' Wolf for a period. "Junia Parker had been working with Howell in Wolf for a while."

podcast.title: Direct Signing with Sun Records
podcast.body: After releasing one single with Modern Records, Parker and his band began recording directly for Sun Records. "But after that one single, Parker and his band started record in directly for son records."

podcast.title: Discovery by Ike Turner
podcast.body: The Blue Flames were discovered by Ike Turner, who initially helped them get signed to Modern Records. "Ike Turner discovered them, and initially got them signed to modern records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Distinguished R&B Career
podcast.body: Junia Parker went on to have a distinguished career in R&B, achieving occasional hit singles until shortly before his death. "Junior Parker would go on to have a distinguished career in R&B, having occasional hit singles until shortly before his death from a brain tumour in 1971."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Poaching by Don Roby
podcast.body: Don Roby, annoyed with Sam Phillips over the "Bearcats" track, poached Little Junior Parker from Sun Records for his own label. Phillips filed an unsuccessful $100,000 lawsuit to prevent this. "Roby signed Parker to an exclusive contract, and even an unsuccessful $100,000 lawsuit from Sam Phillips couldn't stop Roby from having Parker on his label."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Recording at Sam Phillips' Studio
podcast.body: Although signed to Modern Records, Junia Parker and The Blue Flames, like many Modern Records acts, recorded most of their material in Sam Phillips's studio. "though as with many modern records acts, they were recording mostly in Sam Phillips's studio."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: The Beale Streeters Affiliation
podcast.body: Junia Parker was a member of The Beale Streeters, performing alongside blues musicians such as Johnny Ace, Bobby Blueblend, and BB King. "Junia Parker, the blues musician who had been one of the Beale Streeters, with Johnny Ace, Bobby Blueblend, and BB King."
